summary: Community theaters in the city are adopting inclusive casting practices, from open casting policies to adjusted auditions, education programs, reimagined classics, and festivals of original works by diverse playwrights. The note profiles specific initiatives and the people leading them, and reports positive audience response and the use of virtual casting calls and AR previews. It frames these moves as a collective push toward theater that reflects the diversity of society.
one_line: Local community theaters are rolling out inclusive casting policies, auditions, training, reimagined classics and new works to reflect society's diversity.
key_facts: Calloway Community Theater's Artistic Director Jacqueline Smith unveiled the Calloway Inclusive Casting Initiative (CICI) at a town hall meeting on September 15, 2023, for the 2024 season.
The CICI opens roles to actors of all backgrounds, irrespective of race, gender identity, physical ability, or age, as long as they can embody the essence of the character.
Hemsley Auditorium, renowned for musical productions, announced on September 30, 2023 that it is redefining auditions, as stated by Director of Casting Michael Rodriguez.

Michael Rodriguez and his team are implementing workshops to prepare a diverse pool of actors for auditions, aiming to level the playing field and nurture potential rather than just find readymade stars.
Elizabeth Nguyen, a theater veteran and educator, spearheaded the "Stages of Opportunity" program, launched with the Walton Center for Performing Arts on November 2, 2023.
The "Stages of Opportunity" program offers scholarships and mentorship to underrepresented talents.
Penn Street Playhouse announced a reworking of Shakespeare's "Twelfth Night" with a diverse cast, opening January 9, 2024, directed by Henry Owens.
Lakeside Little Theater established a "New Voices Festival," slated to begin February 21, 2024, premiering plays and musicals written and performed by artists of diverse backgrounds.
Christina Ramos is the New Works Coordinator at Lakeside Little Theater and said the festival "is only the beginning."

A recent survey found audiences feel a deeper connection to productions that reflect a multifaceted society; long-time fan Jordan Taylor called inclusive casting "the way forward for community theater."
Many theaters are using virtual casting calls and augmented reality (AR) previews of shows with diverse casts to broaden actor participation.
Savannah Keene, a techie and theater enthusiast, collaborates with local theaters to incorporate these technologies.
